articles.summary: Simply Wall St recap of Forestar's fiscal Q4: sales $580.8M and net income $59.2M, full-year sales $1,635.1M and net income $142.6M, all below the prior year. It also cites a $1.4B land spending plan and Executive Chairman Don Tomnitz's retirement.
articles.why_it_matters: Forestar is D.R. Horton's captive lot developer, so its planned land spend shows how much of Horton's lot need stays in-house rather than going to land bankers like Domain.

articles.summary: Goldman Sachs estimates hyperscalers carry about $3.6 trillion of lease and purchase commitments tied to AI build-outs, part of a $4.1 trillion off-balance-sheet total. Nothing about homebuilders or land.
articles.why_it_matters: No bearing on Domain: the off-balance-sheet commitments are Big Tech data-centre leases, not builder land options.

articles.summary: Forestar reported fiscal Q4 (to Sept 30) revenue of $580.8M, down 13%, and net income of $59.2M, down 32%, on 5,004 lots at a $108,300 average price. Fiscal 2027 guidance: 12,000 to 13,000 lots, $1.4B to $1.5B revenue; liquidity $1.3B.
articles.why_it_matters: D.R. Horton's captive lot supplier is guiding to fewer lot deliveries in fiscal 2027 at falling lot prices (down from $115,700), a read on finished-lot pricing that Domain's option deals compete against.

articles.summary: On Forestar's fiscal Q4 call, CEO Andy Oxley said distressed land opportunities from private builder-developers are increasing and conceded the goal of supplying one-third of D.R. Horton's deliveries is hard; CFO Jim Allen ranked land reinvestment above buybacks.
articles.why_it_matters: Forestar seeing more distressed land from private builder-developers points to private builders short of capital, which is the same pool Domain could approach with land-bank financing.

articles.summary: Forestar's board decided on Oct 28, 2026 that director Samuel R. Fuller will not stand for re-election at the 2027 annual meeting. Stacey H. Dwyer became a director Nov 1, 2026, filling the seat left by Tomnitz's retirement.
articles.why_it_matters: Board turnover at D.R. Horton's lot-development affiliate, with Dwyer seated as a shareholder-designated director, is a contact-list change rather than a shift in how Horton sources lots.

articles.summary: Five Point's Q3 call: $4.4M net loss, $576M liquidity, 16.2% debt to capital, and land sales deferred into 2027 rather than cut prices. Its Hearthstone land-banking arm reported about $3.4B of assets under management, $2.8B fee-paying.
articles.why_it_matters: Hearthstone's $3.4B under management sizes a rival land banker's capacity, and Five Point holding land off the market rather than discounting signals California lot sellers are not yet repricing.

articles.summary: Five Point Holdings revised its full-year 2026 outlook and now expects consolidated net income of about $20 million.
articles.why_it_matters: Same Five Point third-quarter update as the earnings-call item; the lower outlook reflects land sales pushed into 2027 at the owner of rival land banker Hearthstone.

articles.summary: Profile of India's Essar Group and its asset-light strategy after years of deleveraging, including the Essar-backed Mesabi Metallics steel project. No homebuilder or land content.
articles.why_it_matters: No bearing on Domain: an Indian industrial conglomerate's strategy, picked up only for the phrase asset-light.

articles.summary: Crypto-exchange news flash saying Meta, Nvidia and Broadcom have issued up to $300 billion of guarantees for AI data centres and chips, held off balance sheet. Nothing about homebuilders or land.
articles.why_it_matters: No bearing on Domain: the off-balance-sheet exposure is Big Tech AI guarantees, not builder land financing.
